hints.title: Complete String As Own Subsequence
hints.text: The longest possible subsequence of any string is the string itself.

hints.title: Equality vs Discrepancy Invariance
hints.text: If string a equals string b, every subsequence of a is also a subsequence of b, making an uncommon subsequence impossible.

hints.title: Maximum Length Return Rule
hints.text: If string a does not equal string b, the longer string cannot be a subsequence of the shorter string. Simply return max(len(a), len(b)).

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(min(A, B)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all subsequences of a and b takes exponential O(2^N) time for an answer that is statically determined.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single string equality check resolves the problem in O(min(A, B)) time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should demonstrate lateral thinking and explain why the longer string cannot be a subsequence of the other.
